# Config Contract Checklist: Agent model overrides

**Purpose**: Check the requirements for the model file contract, its validation, and its setup
**Created**: 2026-10-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `checklist` procedure based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Depth: standard. Audience: reviewer. Focus: config contract and validation, setup and editing.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the full shape of the model file defined (top-level object, per-agent object, the only two allowed keys)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the allowed agent names, models and efforts listed in one place, so the hook, the change command and the README cannot drift apart? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the behavior defined when the check itself fails to run (for example the hook crashes or Python is missing)? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the content of the error message defined well enough to test (names the bad item, lists the allowed values, names the file)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK005 Is it defined what `st-init` does when `.gitignore` already lists the model file, or when the repo has no `.gitignore`? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is "a Stratum agent" defined in a way a check can test (the plugin-qualified name, not a bare `st-close`)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "reset to default" in the change command defined for one key versus the whole entry? [Clarity, Spec §US4]
- [ ] CHK008 Is it clear that `fable` and `xhigh`/`max` are allowed even though no Stratum agent uses them today? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Do User Story 3 (template on "no") and the Key Entities line (only real overrides go in the file) agree, given the template itself holds three overrides? [Consistency, Spec §US3, decisions D11, D12]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the edge case "a bad entry for one agent blocks every Stratum agent" consistent with FR-006, so non-Stratum agents are never blocked? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-006]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK011 Is a recovery path defined after a blocked start (user fixes the file, then the same step runs again)? [Coverage, Recovery]
- [ ] CHK012 Are existing projects (already set up, no model file) covered, including how they get the template? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the case covered where a subagent, not the main session, starts a Stratum agent? [Coverage, Gap]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK014 Is the assumption that a pre-start hook can change model and effort marked as a blocker that the Plan phase must check first? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the assumption that `haiku` starts Haiku 5.5 checked against the Agent tool's model names? [Assumption]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by the `specify` procedure and the `clarify` procedure
